prediction.text:
Nike's gross margin rose to about 42.8% in Q1 FY2027 from about 42.2% in Q1 FY2026, an increase of about 0.61 percentage points. Nike's 10-Q gives lower warehousing and logistics costs as a favorable driver, worth about 90 basis points. Offsetting items were higher other costs, mainly third-party royalties (about 40 basis points), and a lower NIKE Brand average selling price (about 30 basis points).
Nike's Q1 FY2027 gross margin was about 42.79% (gross profit $4.798 billion on revenue $11.213 billion).
Nike's Q1 FY2026 gross margin was about 42.18% (gross profit $4.943 billion on revenue $11.72 billion).
Gross margin expanded by about 0.61 percentage points year over year, so the margin did increase.
Nike cited lower warehousing and logistics costs as a favorable driver, increasing gross margin approximately 90 basis points.
Nike cited higher other costs, primarily due to third-party royalties, as an offset that decreased gross margin approximately 40 basis points.
Nike cited a lower NIKE Brand average selling price as an offset that decreased gross margin approximately 30 basis points, primarily due to higher discounts and channel mix, partially offset by strategic pricing.

caveats: Only three of the drivers in Nike's gross margin bridge have verified quotes. The worker notes say the same passage also lists other items: favorable foreign exchange, lower NIKE Brand product costs and lower Converse gross margin. Those items are not quoted here, so they are not itemized.
The three quoted drivers net to roughly +20 basis points, which is less than the total increase. The other drivers account for the rest.
Segment-level gross margin commentary (North America, Converse) was not reviewed.
